chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abu al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"We command our young children to combine the first two prayers (Dhuhr and Asr) and the last two prayers (Maghrib and Isha) as long as they remain in a state of ablution, before they become occupied (with other activities)."

key_terms.الصَّلَاتَيْنِ الْأُولَى: The first two prayers (Dhuhr and Asr)

ai.seo_question: How should young children be taught to combine prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the practice of *jam'* (consolidation) for children as a pedagogical tool to ease the transition into full prayer obligation (*taklif*). By combining the midday and afternoon prayers, and the evening and night prayers, while maintaining wudu, the Imam emphasizes the importance of ritual continuity and habituation before the age of discernment. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that early religious training focuses on practical ease and consistency to foster lifelong devotion.
